findings.text: the boundary oracle was rewritten to call reference.py and has been executed at neither revision (logs/accuracy_arm.log is EXIT=137, killed before collection), while the rewrite replaces the old coarse argmin(abs(psi - axis_flux)) plus ternary refinement, which could minimise, with an unconditional global wall maximum via polarity=1 and a different wall source (case["geometry"].wall_points instead of _analytic_inputs), so the BOUNDARY_BUDGET assertion now measures a rule that no run has shown it still passes.

the one-slice call is called launch-bound on the strength of "807 launches in 54.6 ms is 68 us per launch", but 68 us per launch is an order above launch latency and the same page gives the same launch count at 1.27 ms for the unbatched read, so the regime at batch 1 is unsupported by the fragment's own data; the done_when asks for exactly this per-batch classification.

launches_per_call is a count of HLO text lines containing fusion(/custom-call(/call(, not measured kernel launches, and the fragment's "launches" column is read as a runtime count without stating the instrument.

the rebuild=False branch is exercised only by the prototype measure, so the one production change in this diff carries no test that fails if the branch is removed or inverted, and its contract (a caller that knows no lane rebuilds) is unchecked.

the batch test asserts only that one compiled program is reused and never that the batched reading equals the single read, so a vmap that silently changes the reading passes; the owner of this pattern, tests/test_forward_census.py:296, asserts the parity as well.

baseline_suite and after_suite both name logs/negative_control_gpu.log and both name revision 6029edb6b, so the added-failure derivation reads identical text and reports 0 added failures and neither arm is separately addressable, and the recorded arm revision is not the reviewed head 6d2652aa0.
